subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 28-year-old man with metastatic testicular cancer is started on a platinum-based regimen. His oncologist explains that the drug cross-links DNA and is active throughout the cell cycle, regardless of whether cells are dividing.
question: Platinum compounds such as cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin kill cancer cells primarily through which mechanism, and are they cell-cycle specific?

options.text: Inhibition of thymidylate synthase; S-phase specific
Topoisomerase I inhibition; S- and G2-phase specific

explanation_correct: Cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin are platinum compounds that cross-link DNA, forming adducts that block replication and transcription. They are cell cycle nonspecific. They are used for solid tumors — testicular, bladder, ovarian, GI (colorectal), and lung cancers — and for lymphomas. Major toxicities include nephrotoxicity (Fanconi syndrome, prevented with amifostine), peripheral neuropathy, and ototoxicity.

explanation_incorrect.A: Thymidylate synthase inhibition is 5-fluorouracil, which is S-phase specific.
explanation_incorrect.B: DNA intercalation is characteristic of dactinomycin and anthracyclines; bleomycin acts in G2.
explanation_incorrect.D: Microtubule stabilization is the taxane mechanism and is M-phase specific.
explanation_incorrect.E: Topoisomerase I inhibition is irinotecan and topotecan, causing S- and G2-phase arrest.

educationalObjective: Platinum compounds cross-link DNA in a cell-cycle nonspecific manner to treat a wide range of solid tumors.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 60-year-old with ovarian cancer receives cisplatin. After several cycles, laboratory tests show glycosuria, aminoaciduria, and phosphate wasting despite normal blood glucose, and renal function is declining. The oncology team had considered giving a cytoprotective agent before each dose.
question: Which agent can be given to reduce cisplatin nephrotoxicity such as Fanconi syndrome?
explanation_correct: Cisplatin causes nephrotoxicity, including Fanconi syndrome, a proximal tubular dysfunction with glycosuria, aminoaciduria, and phosphate wasting. Amifostine is a free-radical scavenger given prophylactically to reduce platinum-induced nephrotoxicity. Cisplatin also causes peripheral neuropathy and ototoxicity. The prevent-with-amifostine pairing is a classic exam association.

explanation_incorrect.B: Mesna prevents cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide induced hemorrhagic cystitis, not platinum nephrotoxicity.
explanation_incorrect.D: Leucovorin is used for methotrexate rescue and to boost 5-fluorouracil.
explanation_incorrect.E: Allopurinol is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor, not a nephroprotective agent for cisplatin.

educationalObjective: Amifostine is a free-radical scavenger used to prevent cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity including Fanconi syndrome.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 45-year-old receiving cisplatin for bladder cancer reports tinnitus and progressive hearing loss. He also has tingling and numbness in his feet. Audiometry confirms high-frequency hearing loss.
question: Which adverse effect pair is most characteristic of cisplatin?
explanation_correct: Cisplatin's signature toxicities include ototoxicity, with high-frequency hearing loss and tinnitus, and peripheral neuropathy, in addition to nephrotoxicity. These effects are dose limiting and must be monitored. Ototoxicity is especially associated with cisplatin among the platinum compounds. This distinguishes it from busulfan (pulmonary fibrosis), cyclophosphamide (hemorrhagic cystitis), and anthracyclines (cardiomyopathy).

explanation_incorrect.A: Pulmonary fibrosis and hyperpigmentation are busulfan toxicities.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis and bladder cancer are cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide toxicities prevented by mesna.
explanation_incorrect.C: Dilated cardiomyopathy is anthracycline (doxorubicin) toxicity; alopecia is common with etoposide.
explanation_incorrect.E: Constipation and ileus are vincristine neurotoxicities.

educationalObjective: Cisplatin is characterized by ototoxicity, peripheral neuropathy, and nephrotoxicity.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 66-year-old with metastatic colorectal cancer is started on a platinum agent particularly active in GI tumors. A separate patient with ovarian cancer receives a different, better-tolerated platinum agent, and a third with testicular cancer receives the most nephrotoxic platinum agent.
question: Which platinum agent is most specifically associated with the treatment of colorectal (GI) cancers?
explanation_correct: Among the platinum compounds, oxaliplatin is particularly associated with colorectal and other GI cancers, for example in the FOLFOX regimen, whereas cisplatin is strongly linked to testicular and bladder cancers and carboplatin to ovarian cancer. All platinum agents cross-link DNA and are cell-cycle nonspecific. They share nephrotoxicity, neuropathy, and ototoxicity, although carboplatin is generally better tolerated. Matching the specific platinum agent to its classic tumor type is a high-yield distinction.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cisplatin is classically used for testicular and bladder cancers and is the most nephrotoxic and ototoxic platinum agent.
explanation_incorrect.B: Carboplatin is more commonly used for ovarian cancer and is better tolerated than cisplatin.
explanation_incorrect.C: Dactinomycin is an antitumor antibiotic used for Wilms tumor, Ewing sarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ifosfamide is a nitrogen mustard alkylating agent, not a platinum compound.

educationalObjective: Oxaliplatin is the platinum agent most associated with GI/colorectal cancers, whereas cisplatin is linked to testicular/bladder cancer and carboplatin to ovarian cancer.
